argument_markdown:
## Exact theorem (C66-GEO-Z only)

Over any base of balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl data of type F ≅ O(4)⊕O(5) on smooth genus-6 curves, the CE evaluation obstruction for an ordered reduced divisor Γ of degree 6 is entirely carried by the f=5 summand and vanishes if and only if O_C(Γ) ≇ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}. The evaluation-failure locus Z is the finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open of the relative linear system |W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}|.

This is the weakest sufficient identification of Z demanded by the geometric bottleneck. It does not assert that Z is the unique global source of W_{−16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q), nor that contributions supported on Z are Tate.

## Source-backed inputs

1. CE degree formula (SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6, packet primary locator): for W_f = (O_{P(E^∨)}(2) ⊗ γ^* O(−f))|_C one has deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12−4f. The packet and working context both record the minus sign in γ^*O(−f); it is used exactly as stated, not re-derived from first principles beyond the cited degree identity.
2. Canonical geometric bottleneck (packet C66-001-v3): balanced splitting F = O(4)⊕O(5); six-point failure condition O_C(Γ) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}; reduced-support open of the relative degree-six linear system with finite étale S_6 ordering cover (explicitly: do not call that open locus closed).
3. Poincare duality dictionary FND-0001 and degree-26/vcd facts FND-0035, FND-0036 are recorded only as ambient target context. They are not used to construct or identify Z.
4. No dependency artifacts are supplied (dependency_artifacts = {}). No prior attempt IDs are cited.

## Proved steps

### Step A — degrees for g=6
Substitute g=6, f=5 into deg(W_f)=4g+12−4f: deg(W_5)=24+12−20=16. Then deg(W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}) = 16 − (2g−2) = 16−10=6. Likewise deg(W_4)=4·6+12−16=20.

### Step B — obstruction degrees for n=6
SRC-0004 gives deg(ω_C ⊗ W_f^∨(Γ)) = 4f + n − 2g − 14. For (g,n)=(6,6):
- f=5: 20+6−12−14 = 0;
- f=4: 16+6−12−14 = −4.

### Step C — f=4 obstruction vanishes
On a smooth projective curve, a line bundle of negative degree has H^0=0. Thus H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_4^∨(Γ))=0 for every ordered reduced 6-point divisor Γ on every smooth fibre. The f=4 summand never contributes an evaluation failure.

### Step D — f=5 obstruction criterion
The line bundle L_obs := ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ) has degree 0. On a smooth projective curve, a degree-zero line bundle has a nonzero global section if and only if it is trivial. Hence
H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ)) ≠ 0  ⇔  L_obs ≅ O_C  ⇔  O_C(Γ) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}.
(The last equivalence is rewriting L_obs ≅ O_C.) This is exactly the six-point failure condition in the packet, derived from the f_2=5 summand of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 with the stated sign convention.

### Step E — Riemann–Roch lower bound on h^0
Let L := W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}. Then deg L=6, so χ(L)=deg L − g + 1 = 6−6+1=1. Therefore h^0(L)=1+h^1(L) ≥ 1. In particular the relative linear system |L| is nowhere empty on smooth fibres: there is no r=0 stratum for this L. (Stratum geometry for h^0≥2 is deferred to C66-GEO-H0.)

### Step F — construction and identification of Z
Fix a base B of balanced CE data as in the theorem statement, with universal curve π: C→B and relative line bundle L = W_5 ⊗ ω_{C/B}^{−1}.

- Let |L| → B be the relative linear system (Proj of the pushforward of L, or the corresponding Hilbert scheme of fibrewise effective divisors in class L; fibres may jump when h^0 jumps).
- Let |L|_{red} ⊂ |L| be the open locus of divisors that are reduced with six distinct support points on the fibre. (Openness of reduced distinct support in a linear system of degree 6 is the standard open condition on the support; the packet forbids calling this locus closed.)
- Let Z → |L|_{red} be the finite étale S_6-cover that orders the six support points. Equivalently, inside the ordered configuration space C^{[6]}_{ord,red} of distinct fibrewise 6-tuples, define Z as the closed incidence locus of tuples with O_C(∑ p_i) ≅ L|_C.

By Steps C–D, a point of C^{[6]}_{ord,red} has nonzero CE evaluation obstruction if and only if it lies in this incidence locus. By Step C the obstruction is purely the f=5 residual condition. Therefore Z is exactly the evaluation-failure locus for the balanced tetragonal CE problem on ordered distinct markings.

## What is not claimed

- W_5 ≅ ω_C^{⊗2}(−D) for a tetragonal g^1_4 divisor D is a candidate identification in the working context and is not used.
- Dimension, irreducible components, stabilizers, and the map of Z to tetragonal moduli are not determined here (C66-GEO-COMP / C66-GEO-H0).
- The candidate numerical package dim(Hurwitz)=15, dim(Z)=17, codim_M_{6,6}(Z)=4 from the working-context reusable computations is a computational hypothesis only; it is not proved and is not needed for the identification of Z.
- Vanishing of the f=4 summand does not imply that the f=5 residual locus is the unique geometric source of the exact target group (explicitly forbidden by the working-context constraint list).
- No statement is made about Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) or about W_{−16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) being a sum of Q(8).

## Computational hypotheses

None are discharged into the theorem. Finite rank-drop or point-count experiments are not used. The reusable degree arithmetic (sha256 6f4294cbc7166beabebcf00a625753ea71d2e5e71e458ad128f6458235bc972b and 0a749db765a4f0dbac4708d2dd3de1e406f25c54511d5cc9a8d72a152d0a049e in the working context) is re-checked by direct substitution above and treated as elementary arithmetic, not as an external experiment closing a universal claim.

## Gaps (explicit)

1. Full algebraic construction of a Deligne–Mumford moduli stack of balanced tetragonal CE data T^{bal}_6 and of the universal scroll/E is not supplied; the theorem is stated relative to an arbitrary base of such data.
2. Identification of W_5 with a residual canonical bundle ω_C^{⊗2}(−D) is unproved and unused.
3. Component structure, dimensions, and stabilizers of Z are open (downstream subproblems).
4. h^0-stratification of |L| is open (C66-GEO-H0).
5. No Gysin/localization or Tate-type analysis is attempted (C66-TATE-SUPPORT / C66-TATE-ASSEMBLY).

## Failed routes addressed (not reused)

- vcd-only-vanishing: not used. Constructing Z is a geometric incidence construction; FND-0035 already records that (6,6) sits at vcd so vcd-only vanishing cannot settle the target, and it is irrelevant to identifying Z.
- undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex: not used. No graph complex or top-weight decorated/undecorated comparison appears.
- point-count-without-degree-parity-separation: not used. No point counts enter the argument.
- forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown: not used. FND-0036 (forgetful M_{6,6}→M_{6,5}) is ambient context only; Z is not obtained by renaming a local system on a forgetful fibre.

## Relation to the exact target

The campaign target remains: W_{−16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q) ≅ W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)(21) is a direct sum of Q(8). The present lemma only constructs the CE evaluation-failure locus Z through which later subproblems must route the codimension-13 / weight-26 analysis. It neither proves nor disproves the exact target.

summary: Identifies the CE evaluation-failure locus Z for balanced tetragonal (g,n)=(6,6) data as the ordered reduced-support open of |W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}|, after proving f=4 always vanishes and f=5 fails exactly on O(Γ) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}. Does not resolve Tate type of the exact target group, nor components/dimensions/h^0-strata.
theorem_statement: Let B be any base carrying a smooth family of genus-6 curves with balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl data of splitting type F ≅ O_{P^1}(4) ⊕ O_{P^1}(5), and write γ for the scroll projection. Define W_f := (O_{P(E^∨)}(2) ⊗ γ^* O_{P^1}(−f))|_C for f ∈ {4,5} as in SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 (including the minus sign). For an ordered 6-tuple of distinct points (p_1,…,p_6) on a fibre C with Γ = ∑ p_i, the f=4 CE obstruction space H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_4^∨(Γ)) vanishes identically, while H^0(C, ω_C ⊗ W_5^∨(Γ)) is nonzero if and only if O_C(Γ) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}. Consequently the evaluation-failure locus Z over B is precisely the finite étale S_6-cover of the reduced-support open in the relative linear system |W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1}| → B; in particular Z is cut out inside the ordered distinct-point configuration space by the single residual isomorphism condition O(Γ) ≅ W_5 ⊗ ω_C^{−1} coming from the f_2=5 summand.
